Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:12:1.hebrew: אבל פכים קטנים אורחיה - לרבוץ. ואם רבצה עליהן ברה"ר פטור, וברשות הניזק חייבת נזק שלם, דתולדה דרגל הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:12:1.english: But [for] small vessels, [it is] its manner - to crouch. And if it crouched upon them in the public domain, [it is] exempt, and in the domain of the injured party, it is liable [for] full damages, for it is a subcategory of Foot.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:13:1.hebrew: לימא מסייע ליה הבהמה מועדת למעך כו' - ומתניתין קתני דאינה מועדת לרבוץ, אלא ודאי דמתניתין בגדולים, וברייתא בכלים קטנים ובילדים קטנים ובבהמה קטנה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:13:1.english: Let us say [that this] supports him: An animal is forewarned to crush, etc. - And our Mishnah teaches that it is not forewarned to crouch; rather, certainly [the case of] our Mishnah [is] with large [ones], and the baraita [is] with small vessels, and with small children, and with a small animal.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:14:1.hebrew: דלמא מן הצד - האי דקתני מועדת למעך לאו ברביצה, אלא מן הצד: כשהיא מהלכת ויש בצידה כלים, ממעכתן בינה לכותל. וזו היא שאמרנו הזיקה בגופה דרך הלוכה, דהויא תולדה דרגל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:14:1.english: Perhaps from the side - That which [the baraita] teaches, "[an animal] is forewarned to crush," is not [by] crouching, but rather from the side: when it is walking and there are utensils at its side, it crushes them between itself and the wall. And this is what we said, "[where] it caused damage with its body in the course of its walking," which is a subcategory of Foot.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:1:1.hebrew: כולה רבי טרפון היא - ורישא, לאו בחצר הניזק גמורה עסקינן; משום הכי קתני אינה מועדת. ודקא מחייב ליה אשן ורגל — בחצר המיוחדת לניזק לפירות, ובקרן חצי נזק ותו לא, משום דלשוורים הוא רשות לשניהם, וכרה"ר דמיא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:1:1.english: The entire [mishna] is [in accordance with] Rabbi Tarfon - And [in] the first clause, we are not dealing with a complete courtyard of the injured party; therefore it teaches "it is not forewarned." And that which it holds him liable for Tooth and Foot [is because it is] in a courtyard designated for the injured party for produce, and for Horn, half-damages and no more, because for oxen it is a domain for both of them, and it is like a public domain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:20:1.english: Also the hyena - He adds [this] to those of the Mishnah.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:20:2.english: And Rav Yosef said - [He said this] in another place.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:20:3.hebrew: צבוע זו אפא - ומדמוסיף ר"מ אפא, מכלל דברדלס לאו אפא הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:20:3.english: A hyena [tzavo'a], this is an appa - And since Rabbi Meir adds [the] appa, it follows that [a] bardelas is not [an] appa.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:21:1.hebrew: לא קשיא כו' - דברדלס דמתניתין הוא צבוע זכר, ועליו קאמר רב יוסף: צבוע זו אפא. ור"מ מוסיף אף צבוע נקבה דלא שמיה אפא, ודרב יוסף לאו אדר"מ איתמר אלא בעלמא איתמר, כדתניא: צבוע זכר נעשה כו'. אלמא צבוע זכר משתנה לכמה מינין, הלכך קרי לה ברדלס ונפרזא ואפא. כך מצאתי: לישנא אחרינא, ועיקר הוא: מתני' בצבוע נקבה - ור"מ מוסיף צבוע זכר, ותרוייהו מיקרו אפא, דתניא: צבוע זכר וכו', ומשום דמשתנה לבריה אחרת אצטריך לאוסופי בהדיא. מפי מורי, ולא שמעתי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:21:1.english: It is not difficult, etc. - For the bardelas of our Mishnah is a male hyena, and concerning it Rav Yosef said: "A hyena [tzavo'a], this is an appa." And Rabbi Meir adds also the female hyena, which is not called appa. And [the statement] of Rav Yosef was not said concerning [the baraita of] Rabbi Meir, rather it was said independently, as it is taught [in a baraita]: "A male hyena becomes, etc." Thus, a male hyena transforms into several species; therefore it is called bardelas, and nafreza, and appa. So I found [written]. Another version, and it is the primary [explanation]: Our Mishnah [refers] to a female hyena - and Rabbi Meir adds a male hyena, and both of them are called appa, as it is taught [in a baraita]: "A male hyena, etc." — and because it transforms into another creature, it was necessary to add [it] explicitly. [This was reported] from my teacher, though I did not hear [it directly].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:2:1.english: [That which is] fitting for it — yes - For example, fruits and vegetables.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:2:2.english: That which is not fitting for it - [Such as] garments and vessels.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:2:3.hebrew: לא - דמשונה הוא, וחצי נזק הוא דמשלם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:2:3.english: No - For it is unusual, and it is [only] half-damages that he pays.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:3:1.hebrew: ואי רבי טרפון כו' - הא ודאי לגבי שן רשות הניזק הוא, דהא במיוחדת לניזק לפירות אוקימתה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:3:1.english: And if [it is] Rabbi Tarfon, etc. - This [courtyard] is certainly the domain of the injured party with respect to Tooth, for you established it [as a courtyard] designated for the injured party for produce.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:4:1.hebrew: חמשה תמין הן - נגיחה, נגיפה, נשיכה, רביצה, בעיטה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:4:1.english: Five are innocuous - Goring, pushing, biting, lying down, [and] kicking.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:4:2.hebrew: ואם הועדו חמשתן מועדין - והיינו דקתני: חמשה מועדין. והא דקתני השן מועדת לאכול כו' — לאו אמניינא קאי, אלא הכי קאמר: ושן ורגל מועדין מתחילתן. והא דקתני ושור המועד ושור המזיק ברשות הניזק, הכי קאמר: והיכן העדאתן דשן ורגל? ברשות הניזק: ה"ג: מתקיף לה רבינא: הא קתני לקמן שור המזיק ברשות הניזק כיצד? ולא גרס: חדא דחמשה תנן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:4:2.english: And if they were warned, the five of them are forewarned - And this is what [the Mishnah] teaches: "Five are forewarned." And that which it teaches: "The tooth is forewarned to eat, etc." — [this] does not refer to the count [of five]; rather, this is what it is saying: "And tooth and foot are forewarned from the outset." And that which it teaches: "and the forewarned ox, and the ox that causes damage in the domain of the injured party" — this is what it is saying: And where is the forewarning of tooth and foot? In the domain of the injured party. We read [the text] as follows: Ravina objects to it: "Does it not teach later: 'How [is] the ox that causes damage in the domain of the injured party [forewarned]?'" — and we do not read: "Firstly, for we learned five."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:6:1.hebrew: הא קתני לקמן - בפרק כיצד, דקמפרש לכולהו מועדין דפ"ק, וקמפרש נמי שור המזיק ברשות הניזק כיצד:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:6:1.english: Doesn't [the Mishnah] teach below - In the chapter [entitled] Keitzad, where it explains all the forewarned [damagers] of the first chapter, and it also explains: "An ox that causes damage on the property of the injured party, how so?"

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:6:2.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא איירי - בקרן תמה ברשות הניזק בנזק שלם בפ"ק, היינו דתני פירושא בפ"ב "כיצד", ומפרש פלוגתא דרבי טרפון ורבנן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:6:2.english: Granted, if you say that it discusses - [the case of] an innocuous horn [that gored] on the property of the injured party [paying] full damages in the first chapter, that is why [the Mishnah] teaches the explanation in the second chapter, "How so," and explains the dispute between Rabbi Tarfon and the Rabbis.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:6:3.english: But if you say it does not discuss it - In this chapter.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:6:4.english: What [is] “How so” - To what does it refer?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:9:1.english: And if they were warned, the five of them are forewarned - This is the explanation of "five forewarned [ones]" that we learned in the Mishnah.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:9:2.hebrew: ושן ורגל מועדין מתחילתן - לאו אמניינא קאי, אלא מועדין קתני ואזיל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:9:2.english: And tooth and foot are forewarned from the outset - It does not refer to the count [of five]; rather, [the Tanna] continues teaching [those that are] forewarned.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:9:3.hebrew: וזהו שור המועד - הא דאמרן "ואם הועדו חמשתן מועדים", זהו שור המועד הכתוב בפרשה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:9:3.english: And this is the forewarned ox - That which we said, "and if they were warned, all five of them are forewarned" — this is the forewarned ox written in the [Torah] portion.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:9:4.hebrew: ושור המזיק כו' מחלוקת רבי טרפון ורבנן - בפרק שני, והאדם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:9:4.english: And an ox that causes damage, etc., [is] a dispute between Rabbi Tarfon and the Rabbis - [This is discussed] in the second chapter, and [likewise] "and the person."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 16a:9:5.english: And there are forewarned [animals], etc. - [The baraita] is explaining the latter clause of our Mishnah (and the reason they were not counted together with these is because they are not written [in Scripture] like those).

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 16a:1:1.hebrew: כולה רבי טרפון היא - הכא נמי גרסינן: במיוחדת לאחד מהן לפירות, ולא לזה ולזה לשוורים. תימה, דמשמע הא לשניהם לפירות פטור, וא"כ תיפשוט מהכא דפליגי בקושיא דר' זירא ובפירוקא דאביי, ולעיל (בבא קמא דף יד.) הש"ס מסופק. ולהספרים דגרסי: לזה ולזה לשוורים, קשיא איפכא: דתיפשוט דלא פליגי במיוחדת לשניהם לפירות, דחשיב ליה חצר הניזק אע"פ שיש רשות למזיק להניח שם שורו — כ"ש היכא דאין מיוחדת לשוורים כלל חשיב חצר הניזק, ואע"פ שמיוחדת לשניהם לפירות:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 16a:1:1.english: The entire [mishna] is [in accordance with] Rabbi Tarfon - Here too, we read the text [as]: "designated for one of them for produce, and not for this one and that one for oxen." [This is] astonishing, for it implies that if [it were designated] for both of them for produce, [the damager] would be exempt; and if so, let us resolve from here that they disagree regarding Rabbi Zeira's objection and Abaye's resolution, whereas above (Bava Kamma 14a) the Gemara is uncertain [about this]. And according to the manuscripts that read "for this one and that one for oxen," there is the opposite difficulty: for let us resolve [from here] that they do not disagree regarding [a courtyard] designated for both of them for produce, since [the Gemara] considers it the courtyard of the injured party even though the damager has permission to place his ox there — all the more so where it is not designated for oxen at all, it is considered the courtyard of the injured party, even though it is designated for both of them for produce.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 16a:22:1.hebrew: והוא דלא כרע במודים - לפי שמצוה לכרוע, וכי זקיף — זקיף כחויא, כדאשכחן ברב ששת במסכת ברכות (דף יב: ושם); מדה כנגד מדה, ונעשה נחש. זהו עונשו, שגנאי הוא לו במה שנעשה נחש: גליון: ויש מפרשים משום דאמרינן במדרש שיש עצם בשדרו של אדם שממנו נוצר לעתיד לבא, ואותו עצם חזק וקשה כל כך שאין האש יכול לשורפו; והשתא, כשאותו עצם נעשה נחש, אינו חי לעתיד לבא. ואין סברא לומר שיהא עונש גדול כל כך בשביל עון זה, דהא כל ישראל יש להם חלק לעולם הבא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 16a:22:1.english: And this [applies only] when he did not bow during Modim - Because it is a mitzvah to bow, and when one straightens up, one straightens up like a snake, as we find regarding Rav Sheshet in Tractate Berakhot (12b and there); [therefore, it is] measure for measure, and [his spine] becomes a snake. This is his punishment: that it is a disgrace for him that [it] becomes a snake. Gloss: And some explain [that this is] because we say in the Midrash that there is a bone in a person's spine from which he is recreated in the future to come, and that bone is so strong and hard that fire cannot burn it; and now, when that bone becomes a snake, he will not live in the future to come. However, it is not reasonable to say that there would be such a great punishment for this sin, for all Israel has a share in the World to Come.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 16a:2:1.hebrew: ראוי לה אין, שאין ראוי לה לא - אין להקשות דלמא הא דקאמר "מועדת" היינו לשלם מן העלייה, ושאין ראוי לה, אע"פ שמשלם נ"ש כר' טרפון, אינו מועד לשלם מן העלייה, כדאמרינן בפ"ב (דף יח:); ולשון "מועד" שייך על זה, כדאמרינן: הידוס אינו מועד, ויש אומרים מועד, ובהא קמיפלגי, דמר סבר מגופו ומר סבר מן העלייה — דע"כ שאין ראוי לה לא משלם כי אם חצי נזק, דלקמן בפ"ב (בבא קמא דף יט:) בהדיא קתני גבי "השן מועדת": אכלה כסות או כלים, משלמת חצי נזק:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 16a:2:1.english: [What is] fitting for it — yes; [what is] not fitting for it — no - One should not object: Perhaps that which [the Mishnah] says "forewarned" means to pay from the best [property], whereas [for] what is not fitting for it, even though one pays full damages according to Rabbi Tarfon, it is not [considered] forewarned to pay from the best [property], as we say in the second chapter (18b); and the term "forewarned" is applicable to this, as we say [there]: "Hopping is not forewarned, and some say it is forewarned," and they disagree on this, as one Master holds [it pays] from its own body and one Master holds [it pays] from the best [property] — for perforce, [for] what is not fitting for it, one only pays half damages, as later in the second chapter (Bava Kamma 19b) it explicitly teaches regarding "The tooth is forewarned": "If it ate clothing or vessels, it pays half damages."
